title: Output swing, slew rate and full-power bandwidth

sections.heading: The idea
sections.body_md:
Two limits stop an op-amp output from following a large, fast signal. The **output swing** cannot exceed the supply rails (minus a headroom). The **slew rate** \(SR\) caps how fast the output can change, because the internal compensation capacitor is charged by a limited current.

Slewing is non-linear. A small-signal bandwidth limit rounds a sine but keeps it a sine; slewing turns the steep parts into straight ramps, creating a triangle-like shape. A sine of amplitude \(V_p\) has maximum slope \(\omega V_p\), so above a certain frequency a full-amplitude sine cannot be reproduced. That frequency is the **full-power bandwidth**.

sections.heading: Key equations
sections.body_md:
Ramp time for a large step: \(t = \dfrac{\Delta V}{SR}\)
Maximum slope of \(V_p\sin\omega t\): \(\omega V_p\).
\[ f_{FP} = \frac{SR}{2\pi V_p} \]
Slewing starts when the needed slope exceeds \(SR\); small steps may never slew.
sections.figure_alt: A dashed ideal sine wave and a solid output waveform whose steep parts are replaced by straight ramps, looking triangular.

sections.heading: Worked example
sections.body_md:
An op-amp has \(SR = 2\ \mathrm{V/\mu s}\). A 6 V step takes about \(6/2 = 3\ \mu\mathrm{s}\) to ramp. For a full-swing sine of \(V_p = 8\ \mathrm{V}\):
\[ f_{FP} = \frac{2\times10^{6}}{2\pi\times8} \approx 39.8\ \mathrm{kHz} \]
At 20 kHz an 8 V sine passes cleanly; at 100 kHz only about 3.2 V peak would.

sections.heading: Common pitfalls
sections.body_md:
- Multiplying instead of dividing for ramp time.
- Using peak-to-peak instead of peak amplitude in \(f_{FP}\).
- Treating slew distortion as a linear filtering effect.
- Forgetting the \(2\pi\) when converting rad/s slope to Hz.

sections.heading: Where this leads
sections.body_md: Slew rate, output swing and GBW together decide whether a part can handle a given signal; datasheet questions often combine them. When a waveform looks triangular on a scope, suspect slewing before suspecting bandwidth.
